workload: 30k cells x 800 genes sparse counts, 200 donors x 40 cell types, 12 donor-constant metadata columns
notes: Most of the runtime is the Python per-profile scan that decides which obs columns are constant (about 1.05s of 1.18s on this shape). One argsort of the profile ids plus a reduceat answers the same question in about 0.02s and leaves the aggregated matrix unchanged. Open PRs 1023/1022/986 do not touch this file.

workload: 4000 cells x 3000 count-like genes, 40 signatures of 50 genes, n_up = top 5 percent
notes: The CPU kernel calls scipy.stats.rankdata once per cell, but the recovery curve only uses ranks <= n_up. Ranking is most of the call (about 0.6s of 0.8s on a similar matrix). A batched top-k ordinal rank (argpartition, stable tie break only on the boundary) feeds the same numba AUC and drops that per-cell Python loop. tests/test_es_methods.py exercises it through ov.es.aucell. Not in any open upstream PR.

workload: 30000 cytometry events x 20 markers, 10x10 SOM, 6 epochs, full-matrix batch
notes: Each epoch builds an (n_events, n_nodes, n_markers) squared-distance temporary. The same BMU indices come from ||x||^2 + ||c||^2 - 2 x c^T, which was about 15x faster on one pass of this shape (0.28s vs 0.019s) and does not allocate the 3-D block (tracemalloc peak of a 2-epoch run was ~605MB). tests/flow/test_flowsom.py covers SOM.train via flowsom. Not in any open upstream PR.

workload: 4000 spatial spots, 8 cell types, 6 distance bins (one Visium capture)
notes: co_occurrence calls scipy.spatial.distance_matrix and then builds a boolean within-radius mask, so peak memory is several dense n x n blocks (tracemalloc 626090575 bytes, identical across 5 runs; the distance matrix alone is 128MB). Pair counts can be accumulated in row blocks with cdist, same radii and same statistic, at O(block * n) memory. tests/space/test_neighborhood.py covers the function (squidpy parity skips when squidpy is absent). Not in any open upstream PR.
